entries.text: Wanting something weightier than a stock whoosh for a flying witch, he pitched down a recording of his old washing machine and added reverb. His library is tagged both by source and by what each sound evokes, which surfaces surprises.

entries.text: For Errol Morris’s The Fog of War, Anderson coaxed a feedback loop out of a child’s toy microphone and pitched it down into a slow, dreamlike clicking pulse — darkly ironic under footage of napalm.

source.title: Coll Anderson Special: Documentary Sound

entries.text: On Catfish the team kept phone calls gritty and let editor-planned cuts stay audibly rough. The story was already hard to believe, so the raw sound kept reminding viewers this was real footage.

source.title: Coll Anderson Special: Documentary Sound

entries.text: In Restrepo, calm nature beds let the audience feel the soldiers’ boredom, making the sudden lurch into distorted chaos hit harder. The ambiences also told viewers where shots came from and where each soldier stood.

source.title: Coll Anderson Special: Documentary Sound

entries.text: Anderson works on two levels at once: a realistic surface the audience accepts as fact, and underneath it emotional, dreamlike sounds that stretch reality — what he calls sonic irony — so you hear how the story feels.

entries.text: Wakanda’s technology mixes high-tech layers with organic, African-rooted sources: the signature flyby of one ship is an African bird recording slowed way down, with Kontakt used for layering and pitch work.

source.title: Behind the roaring sound of 'Black Panther'

entries.text: The Royal Talon Fighter was split into three jobs: air displacement whooshes for size and speed, pitched tonal propulsion, and mechanical fin movement to ground it. Propulsion came in two or three separable layers so one could be chosen to sit with the final score.

source.title: Behind the roaring sound of 'Black Panther'

entries.text: Early VFX made bullets look like ricochets off the Panther suit, but the intent was absorption. So metallic hits were reversed and layered with contact sounds, making rounds seem to thud into the suit and drop.

source.title: Behind the roaring sound of 'Black Panther'

entries.text: For Black Panther’s spirit-world scenes he found an endlessly evolving Reaktor tone whose pitch sometimes harmonized with the score and sometimes drifted against it — beautiful but subtly unsettling.

source.title: Behind the roaring sound of 'Black Panther'

entries.text: In the waterfall challenge fights the falls had to feel powerful without exhausting ears, so their presence was pulled back to let Foley, dialogue and many added effort sounds connect the audience to the fighters.

source.title: Behind the roaring sound of 'Black Panther'

entries.text: On Black Panther’s mix, music ducked around dialogue, and wherever an effect and a cue fought for the same frequency range, the effect took over that space rather than both being turned down.

source.title: How an experimental process created the sensation of hearing loss for 'Sound Of Metal'

entries.text: To capture Ruben’s inner world in Sound of Metal, Becker put sensitive mics on Riz Ahmed’s chest for breath and heartbeat, a tiny mic inside his mouth, and a geophone on his scalp for low-frequency bone vibration.

source.title: How an experimental process created the sensation of hearing loss for 'Sound Of Metal'

entries.text: In the pharmacy scene the footsteps aren’t feet hitting the floor but the resonance of Ruben’s own body, so the audience hears walking the way a person with failing ears would feel it.

source.title: How an experimental process created the sensation of hearing loss for 'Sound Of Metal'

entries.text: Once Ruben learns sign language, Becker deliberately strips the design back, leaving the audience as lost as Ruben and avoiding the fatigue of constant subjective processing.

source.title: Creating The Poetic Sci-Fi Sound Of 'Arrival'

source.title: Creating The Poetic Sci-Fi Sound Of 'Arrival'

entries.text: Arrival’s alien logograms were built from Foley of vegetables and rice moving in water, plus metal brushes scraped across a plastic board — deliberately organic sources instead of an electronic sci-fi palette.

source.title: Creating The Poetic Sci-Fi Sound Of 'Arrival'

entries.text: For a subtly shifting atmosphere, the team chopped wind recordings into tiny fragments and intercut them with fragments of unrelated winds, then kept the result low in the mix so it was felt more than noticed.

source.title: Creating The Poetic Sci-Fi Sound Of 'Arrival'

entries.text: Arrival’s flashbacks use natural sound with no pitching or processing; instead sounds from the present bleed into the past and back, with gentle fader moves and light EQ tying the timelines together.

source.title: Creating The Poetic Sci-Fi Sound Of 'Arrival'

entries.text: Radios and comms devices in Arrival were made by playing dialogue through real speakers and re-recording it, rather than faking it with EQ or futz plug-ins.

source.title: Creating The Poetic Sci-Fi Sound Of 'Arrival'

entries.text: A helicopter clashed with Jóhann Jóhannsson’s score in the same frequency band, so the team reshaped its pitch and harmonics until it threaded through the music while still reading as a helicopter.

entries.text: Severance’s stuttering ‘fritz’ began in Theodore Shapiro’s score; Ribicoff studied the waveform frame by frame and hand-cut a sound in Pro Tools to the same one-two-frame pattern, then reused it on effects like the elevator transitions.
